selections.comment: A lightly-raced mare who beat a solid yardstick at Roscommon, LA NOTE VERTE can follow up. Tailed off on her racecourse debut on heavy ground at Fairyhouse in March 2024, the Willie Mullins-trained five-year-old has remained unbeaten in three subsequent starts. Winning with any amount in hand recently, the daughter of Australia has the potential to improve further provided she settles better on this stiff track. Having landed four of her six outings over flights, Emily Love is a battle-hardened mare who won't be easily beat. She deserves maximum respect. Avondale and the unbeaten Timeless Treaty are also of interest.

selections.comment: Twice placed in Grade 1 races over hurdles, the Gordon Elliott-trained KING OF KINGSFIELD can make the breakthrough over fences. Runner-up at Navan last November on his only previous run in this discipline, the seven-year-old should be able to make his class count. Having adopted pacemaking duties for much of last season, he is likely to be ridden with more restraint on this occasion. A 143-rated hurdler, the son of Vadamos is an exciting prospect for this time of the year. A bumper and novice hurdle winner at the track, My Great Mate is sure to have been campaigned with this meeting in mind and shouldn't be far away under Paul Townend. Tipperary runner-up Jet Setting Jim is another with leading claims.

selections.comment: Having only got the hang of things late on when third on her debut at Leopardstown, AMELIA EARHART can improve past runner-up Thenandnow. Sent off a well-backed favourite, the Aidan O'Brien-trained filly ran green over a furlong out before keeping on late. She should know a bit more on this second start. Thenandnow was always front rank before sticking to her task under Shane Foley. From a favourable low draw, the Dubawi filly is sure to be up with the pace from the outset. Given that Paddy Twomey trained the winner of that Leopardstown race, his representative Black Caviar Gold has to be respected.

selections.comment: Second in this last year, NORWALK HAVOC can go one place better. Winner of a Listed race at Leopardstown subsequently, the Jessica Harrington-trained four-year-old looks to have been campaigned with a repeat bid in mind. Following a promising reappearance in a Group 3 last month, the son of Showcasing should be primed for this contest. A prominent racer, he is much more favourably drawn than he was 12 months ago. Slieve Binnian, who has been a revelation for connections in recent weeks, looks a serious threat. The David Marnane-trained gelding quickened up smartly to win a premier handicap at Leopardstown last time. Mississippi River is also worthy of consideration in a typically competitive renewal.

selections.comment: COLLECTING COIN can get off the mark at the third time of asking. The Jessica Harrington-trained gelding finished third on his racecourse debut at Cork back in April, before going down narrowly at the Curragh the following month. In a race where most of the leading contenders appear relatively exposed, the son of Lope De Vega looks one of few potential improvers. Unlucky in running at Limerick recently, Gran Habano should be competitive. Less than a length behind the selection at the Curragh, there is unlikely to be much between the pair again. Adieu Spirit is a newcomer worth keeping an eye on in the betting.

selections.comment: Following a promising reappearance at Killarney, IMPOSING SUPREME should be primed for this contest. Third last year, the Tom Gibney-trained grey justified favouritism when successful here a few days later. A dual winner at the meeting back in 2021, the nine-year-old always deserves maximum respect at Ballybrit. Alpha Capture seems another who has been campaigned with this meeting in mind. Runner-up here last year, the Willie Mullins-trained gelding was unlucky on his return at Leopardstown. While he had no obvious excuses at Killarney last time, there will be plenty who give him another chance. Summer Snow should be suited to this track, while reserve On A Session would be of interest if getting a run.

selections.comment: SPECKLED MEADOW has each-way claims in a wide-open affair. Runner-up last year, the Don Browne-trained mare is a previous winner at this track. There was plenty to like about her recent comeback effort at Leopardstown, where she stayed on late into mid-division. Granted normal improvement from that first start since November, the eight-year-old should be competitive. Loingseoir has shaped well enough of late to suggest he still retains plenty of ability at this level. Nicola Burns is a positive jockey booking on the veteran. Just For One Day would have every chance if behaving herself in the stalls and breaking on terms.

Paco's Pride is the most experienced horse in the race here, she has some decent 2024 form and although this term looks poor if getting back to last years can get amongst it here. Making up the places Cuda Been A Rowlex, he has won before which is more than can be said for any other rival, so has to be considered in what looks a weak race.

He's only 1lb higher here and with the slightly longer trip in his favour is fancied to get the better of Oldbury Lad who goes the other way in distance having failed to get home over 7f last time. That rival was in good form over sprint trips in the spring and is one of the least exposed in the field. Veteran Diamondsinthesand has been out of form in 2025 but continues to drop in the weights and could complete the tricast.

selections.comment: A strong renewal with plenty of Royal Ascot and Group form on offer. The highly regarded Zavateri travelled best when taking the July Stakes last time benefitting from a strong gallop and is bred to get 1m in time so is hugely respected. He finished ahead Do Or Do Not who backed up his Coventry run but couldn't go the early pace before flying home when meeting the rising ground suggesting that this longer trip would deliver more. He can get closer to his conqueror that day and confirm Ascot form with Andab. Humidity is 2-2 landing the Chesham last time and likely has more to offer. However that didn't look the strongest renewal of the contest and he could be vulnerable to a classier rival. DORSET is yet to try Group company but he quickened clear impressively last time when beating a potentially classy stablemate who has won decisively since. He represents a top yard which has won a couple of renewals of this in the last decade and is open to plenty of improvement on just his third start so gets a narrow verdict in an open race for the grade.

selections.comment: A strong renewal with the last couple of winners re-opposing in Audience and KINROSS. The former got the better of the latter last year but he had the run of the race from the front and got first run that day and faces more competition for the lead here. He may struggle to confirm form with the 2023 winner who has proven admirably consistent for a number of years at the top level over 6-7f. Prior to that he finished runner up in the French Guineas following a Greenham victory and he could have more to offer now returned to a suitable trip. Lake Forest was unsuited by the way the race developed behind Quinault last time but holds a chance if back to the form of his Australian victory in the autumn.

selections.comment: Aidan O'Brien has a stranglehold at the top of the market here with ILLINOIS and Scandinavia. The latter was an impressive Bahrain Trophy winner last time relishing the fast ground and long straight shooting himself to the top of the Leger market. With more to come over staying trips he is hugely respected but this track may not play to his strengths as much and Ryan Moore opts to ride his stablemate who is preferred. The selection was only narrowly denied at the top level in the 2024 Leger by a stablemate who has franked the form in the Coronation Cup and he came a long way clear of the remainder when runner up to a useful yardstick in the Gold Cup last time. He was outstayed by a good yardstick that day but should have more to offer dropped back to 2m given his previous Ormonde win has been boosted by the runner up. Sweet William was also outstayed at Royal Ascot but finished runner up in this last year so can compete for the final place with Dubai Future who was a long way behind the selection last time at Ascot. However he only finished a place behind that rival and will likely be ridden to pick up the pieces once again.

He went too fast last time but is just 2lb above last winning mark and could spring a surprise.

selections.comment: Bottom weight BLESSED STAR is very interesting here returned to handicaps off a potentially lenient mark. She met trouble when runner up to a useful rival who has franked the form in a better race last time and is entitled to come on for that first outing of the year. Though she was held off this mark in a nursery last year she is clearly an improved horse this term and it would be no surprise to see her resuming positive tactics from a good draw. The progressive Mahra's Love is the opponent most feared also possessing a handy draw given her impressive win from the front last time where she showed an excellent turn of foot off just 6lb lower. Dash Of Azure backed up her AW win with a fine effort in the Sandringham last time despite racing away from the action in the centre of the track. If in the same form here she should be on the premises once again as well.

She runs off the same mark as when she won at Catterick last time, which should see her win here and land another race this season. Gentle Warrior was a winner off the very low mark of 58 back in October; he has been creeping up the weights slightly without actually winning, therefore he will no doubt run well here and claim another place spot. And Silver Chamber hails from a powerful yard that is in form at present; she is yet to win but can build on that 2nd place effort from last time and fill the places here.

selections.comment: CANARIA QUEEN was a nice enough winner of a classified stakes at Nottingham last time out over the 5-furlong trip; she runs in a similar race here to last time and is only 1 lb higher in the weights after that victory. She was pretty prominent throughout and soon led with 1 furlong to go, always doing enough when out in front and maybe just getting a touch lonely when getting there. She ultimately won by a head in the end, and if she is in the same form here as then, she could be hard to peg back as she looks for back-to-back career successes for the first time. Latin Five was an unlucky loser last time, and although he did manage to finish 3rd, he was unlucky because he did not get a clear run with a furlong to go when making nice headway but still ran on in the closing stages. With a bit more luck in running, he could do well and claim 2nd spot here. And Mrs Bagerran has been running pretty well at present; he can go well here and fill the places.

selections.comment: ABLOOM comes from the William Haggas yard, which currently operates around the 35% win strike rate mark for the last 14 days, and their runner here looks like she is going to get off the mark very soon. Unraced as a 2-year-old last season, she has run four times this season already, putting in enough performances earlier on in the season before coming 2nd on her last two runs. That includes a 2nd at Newmarket last time behind Azaniya, who has since gone on to win again, this time at Windsor. Her main rival has to carry a penalty here; therefore, the Haggas horse could finally get off the mark at the fifth attempt. Ferrari Gold was a nice winner on her second ever start at Chester last time; she does have to carry a penalty here for that win; therefore, that could be the difference maker between 1st and 2nd here. And Renewal is the only runner in this race to run as a youngster last year; she looked as if she needed the seasonal debut run last time, and she could come on for that run and place in this contest.
